title: Shipped it: FLUX.2 art, hand-built engine
author: Professional-Tie3286
selftext:
Rhythm Orbits went live on Google Play this week. Since this sub is about the workflow, here is where AI carried the project and where it was useless.
    
    What AI produced: the whole visual layer. Eleven world backgrounds with parallax stacks, the crystal HUD set, eight orb pairs, tile atlases, store art — all FLUX.2 [turbo] through fal.ai. The menu track is Suno, commercially licensed.
    
    What it could not touch: timing. Judging windows, beat maps, the 185 ms minimum gap between inputs, the count-in, the server-side time-trial clock. None of that survives being guessed at. All 110 levels are validated by a bot that must clear them cleanly before the build passes.
    
    The real cost was not generation, it was normalisation. Generated orb art comes back at wildly different framings. I normalise on equal-area disc rather than bounding box — one spiky pair fills 97% of its canvas while its actual sphere matches everything else, and normalising on extent shrinks that sphere by an eighth.
    
    Second lesson: check the alpha channel before every cutout. Delivered assets are often already transparent, and re-cutting destroys glow and antialiasing.
    
    https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.rhythmorbits.app
    
    Happy to go deeper on the asset pipeline or the level validator.

comments.body: isn't this a literal dance of fire and ice clone?

replies.author: Professional-Tie3286
replies.body: Fair comparison. It shares the one-button, path-based rhythm premise with ADOFAI. Rhythm Orbits is independently built and adds its own mechanics and modes, but I’m not going to pretend the resemblance isn’t there.
